title: Flagged by the Machine: How Google Ads Suspended an Open-Source macOS Term as Malicious
gist: Google Ads suspended the ad account of the creator of RACE, an open-source Rust macOS terminal multiplexer, as 'malicious software' even though the app was Apple-notarized, rated clean by Google Safe Browsing and Search Console, and had zero VirusTotal hits. The appeal loop was circular, and the account was reinstated only after the case spread on Hacker News, with no explanation. The author argues that behavioural black-box scanners structurally penalize legitimate low-level developer tools.

insights.claim: Google Ads flagged RACE's documentation and download domain for malicious software even though the binary was Apple-notarized, Google Safe Browsing and Search Console reported it clean, and VirusTotal showed zero positives.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Google's own safety systems disagree with each other, so false-positive risk for developer tools is high and hard to predict.
insights.quote: Despite distributed release binaries passing native operating system notarization and independent antimalware inspections

insights.claim: Google Ads' appeal process was circular: appeals were rejected deterministically without disclosing the triggering hash, rule or artefact, and account support required the security suspension to be resolved first.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Opaque automated enforcement creates regulatory exposure for Google under EU platform rules and costs small developers customer acquisition.
insights.quote: Seeking account support was blocked by prerequisites that the underlying security suspension must be resolved first.
insights.locator: Attempts to remediate the suspension uncovered

insights.claim: The suspension was reversed only after the case trended on Hacker News, and Google still gave no explanation. Community escalation, not the formal process, was what actually worked.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Developers without a public platform have little recourse against automated takedowns, which concentrates risk on small vendors.
insights.quote: Still no explanation of what triggered the suspension
insights.locator: Through the apparent magic of Hacker News

insights.claim: Kaminski says he will keep contesting the suspension on all available paths, including the EU Court.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Individual cases like this feed the EU's push for transparency in platform automated decision-making.
insights.quote: he will continue his fight on all possible paths, even in the EU Court.
insights.locator: The case illustrates the systemic tension

themes.theme: Why legitimate systems tools look like malware

insights.claim: Terminal multiplexers that keep child shells alive across UI restarts by forking orphaned background workers that accept arbitrary command input share behavioural signatures with backdoors and remote access trojans.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Heuristic scanners will keep producing false positives on process-managing dev tools, which adds friction to distribution.
insights.quote: an executable that persistently forks orphaned background workers capable of receiving arbitrary command-line input shares behavioural signatures with persistent backdoors
insights.locator: Automated security scanners evaluate binary safety

insights.claim: RACE is a Rust terminal multiplexer for macOS that replaces tmux-style grids with an infinite canvas and separates command execution from window lifecycles through a PTY host daemon or a dtach backend.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Shows ongoing innovation in native developer terminal tooling.
insights.quote: RACE differs from conventional grid-based terminal multiplexers such as tmux by implementing an infinite canvas architecture

insights.claim: As platforms rely more on black-box behavioural models, developers of native utilities that manage processes, memory maps or kernel hooks will face more friction across distribution and commercial infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Systems-level developer tool vendors will need to budget for compliance work such as documented process topologies and isolated workers.
insights.quote: developers building legitimate native utilities that manage processes, manipulate memory maps, or hook low-level kernel abstractions face growing friction
insights.locator: The case illustrates the systemic tension

insights.claim: The author recommends that teams shipping developer binaries expect false positives by documenting process topologies and separating persistent worker agents from the main UI binary. RACE 1.0.39 added explicit prompts and cleanup hooks for orphaned processes.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Architecture choices for desktop dev tools are now partly driven by how scanners will judge them.
insights.quote: Engineering teams distributing developer-focused binaries must anticipate false positives by documenting process topologies
insights.locator: The case illustrates the systemic tension
